features.name: Motion / Transform Keyframes
features.summary: Edit property keys, spatial position handles and value/velocity graphs on the same editable project. Curve the route between paired positions while retaining ordinary history, saving and final compilation.
features.purpose: Create deliberate editable movement and retain the same keys across manual editing, Director proposals, saving and final compilation.
available_to: signed-in users with owned project and applicable entitlement
workflow: Open Motion → Transform keyframes and choose the Target layer. Read X, Y, Scale, Rotate and Opacity at the playhead. Scroll down for keyframes, value/easing fields and the separate Start/End velocity and influence controls.
Show motion keyframes in the timeline and expand an ordinary visual layer or graphic group, including targets without animation keys.
Edit an unanimated property value and commit with Enter or blur; Escape cancels. Add the individual property key at the playhead to start animation.
Move the playhead and edit that animated property to write its next key. Inspect evaluated values and use previous/next keys, timeline nudges and the existing easing/curve inspector.
At each playhead position, inspect X, Y, Scale, Rotate, Opacity and Crop X/Y for the evaluated pose. A zero-opacity key displays 0% in Motion.

Drag empty property-lane space to box-select across expanded rows. Shift/Ctrl/Command adds; Alt subtracts; Escape or pointer cancellation restores the prior selection. Shift/Ctrl/Command-click also selects individual keys. Drag, frame-nudge, scale spacing, apply interpolation or delete with the batch toolbar.

Copy with the toolbar or Ctrl/Command+C. Choose Original layers or an existing visual layer in Paste to, then paste at the playhead with the toolbar or Ctrl/Command+V. A single-source-layer clipboard can target another layer; supported property values, spacing, easing and curves are retained with fresh key identities.

Owning-track locks prevent changes. Group values use their own five-property bounds; group key selection opens Composite with the shared curve editor. Undo/redo, save/reopen, render and inspect the current output. Static anchor geometry is not an animated property.

In Motion, Add position key writes an X/Y pair at the playhead. Drag a path point over the picture or nudge with Arrow keys (Shift increases the step). The picture follows the temporary drag; release commits the pair once, while Escape/cancellation restores the prior edit. Paths sample actual X/Y interpolation and map animated parent coordinates.

Select a timeline key, open Graph editor and choose Value graph or Velocity graph. Edit the interval arriving at that key. Signed velocity uses property units per programme second; endpoint influence preserves endpoint velocity. Numeric edits commit on Enter/blur and write the existing four cubic handles.
Once a transform is animated, Motion inspector value edits write a key at the playhead. The static fallback is retained for the base transform; it no longer overrides visible key-driven values.
Editing motion keys while viewing a completed movie switches After to Live Edit. The prior download remains available through Export; it is not presented as an updated movie.

For paired position keys, select the layer in Motion → Transform keyframes, place the playhead in the interval and choose Curve path. Drag or arrow-nudge the amber handles; release commits once and Escape cancels. Straighten path retains its endpoints. Check the changed route before export.
features.preview_behavior: Evaluates canonical layer/group property keys on the existing preview clock. Keyed images take precedence over legacy CSS entrance animations and transitions. Nested groups apply evaluated parent transforms after child composition and clamp curve overshoot to the group control bounds. Broad raster, media, curves and continuous playback agreement remains unqualified.
features.render_behavior: Uses the existing shared compiler/compositor and interpolation expressions where supported. Group keys retain canonical target ownership and are projected into the group composition plan; output time maps back to the programme clock. Inspect the actual exported movie; the status does not certify every combination.
limitations: This dated development snapshot does not establish professional or production readiness.

Two bounded masked image-effect edits preserve eight position/scale/rotation/opacity keys through native save/reopen/export. Inverted-polygon sampled picture passes; one ellipse raster pair still exceeds the strict colour bound. This does not qualify every mask/easing/media or legacy entrance clock.

One native nested image/two-motion project preserves 16 group keys across eight channels, including one custom X Bézier curve. Midpoint, property rows, nudge/lock, reset/remove/undo, save/cold reopen, CPU export and full timeline playback pass; four image geometry pairs pass and decoded source-tone audio is unchanged. Native retiming, broader curves, broader mask/blend combinations, video/owned 3D/deeper groups, full raster and live sound remain unqualified. Existing worker Bézier expressions approximate 32 samples; browser interpolation solves the curve.

Cross-layer paste requires a single source layer and a current-project destination supporting every copied property and value range. Missing targets, unsupported crop/group bounds, destination locks, half-frame timing collisions and programme overflow reject the whole paste. Original-layers mode supports mixed owners. Clipboard is local to this timeline component; it is not an OS/project interchange format. Freehand lasso and cross-project interchange are not qualified. Broad media/retiming/full picture and sound qualification remains open.

Velocity/influence edits write a custom cubic curve, including when converting an easing preset. Flat intervals cannot acquire movement through velocity alone. Influence is1–99%; speeds that exceed the supported handle range reject. Hold has a discontinuous step and no finite editable endpoint velocity. Worker custom curves retain the existing32-sample approximation.

Spatial handles are endpoint-relative position offsets, bounded to ±200 composition percent. The route uses paired neighboring X/Y keys; other keys retain their existing interpolation. Adding or retiming individual keys can change adjacent intervals. Automatic arc-length speed, roving keys, closed vector contours and vector-shape morphs are not provided by these handles.

Curved intervals share a sampled travel curve in preview and export. Travel progress stays on the authored route; it is distinct from constant screen-distance speed. Native proof covers one image and four intervals; broader retiming, animated parents, other media and whole picture/sound remain unqualified.

Choose the brand name, accent, background and an 8–14 second duration that fits the programme. Build editable logo motion at the programme start.

For an image with a left-hand symbol and separate lettering, enable Separate left symbol from wordmark. Symbol width places the search boundary; the builder follows transparent space and rejects cuts through opaque artwork. Three separately masked fragments assemble the symbol, which accelerates along forward routes before joining the original wordmark.

Enable Construct words from pieces to assemble the original bitmap wordmark from 2–16 interlocking slices. Five words each construct from three independently masked title pieces, with staggered rebounds before a continuous close.

Choose Piece choreography: Spring assembly keeps the symbol-first interlocking arrangement; Diamond cascade opens with four triangular pieces per word, moves each complete word into place, then assembles the original logo in centre-out diagonal slices.

features.preview_behavior: The builder writes ordinary graphics into the existing project. SVG shapes become raster artwork. Raster identities can use three reveal bands, or separate symbol and original wordmark along a transparent seam. Separated symbols assemble through three ordinary polygon-masked fragments, then use one continuous symbol during camera travel. With a background, a dark stage resolves to a light field. Both treatments finish on one continuous original lockup. Ordinary preview evaluates existing transforms, masks and opacity keys. Piece construction crops the original decoded RGBA into narrow image slices without redrawing the wordmark. Each slice has two complementary masks. Create., Schedule., Publish., Move and forward. each assemble from three zigzag-masked ordinary text layers; matching continuous titles replace the settled fragments. Diamond cascade is a second authoring arrangement of the same native graph. It uses four triangular masks per word, large opening type, continuous word travel and a centre-out original-logo assembly; Spring assembly remains unchanged.

limitations: Three editable deterministic symbol families, not an unrestricted AI brief generator or automatic tracing of uploaded logos. Bundled A–Z/a–z letters, numbers, spaces, ampersand, period and hyphen; 1–32 characters, Inter 600/900.

Each outlined letter is a vector layer after creation. Change its contours or build a new wordmark from the name field; it is not a live text object and does not retain an editable text-to-outline binding.

Compound artwork supports one to eight contours, 2–64 points per contour (three if closed), at most 256 total. Overlapping fills use even-odd parity. This does not add boolean operations or contour morph animation.

Master downloads use a flat logo group, vector geometry and base transforms before motion. Masks, crops, rounded frames, glows, shadows and blends must be removed; nested or non-vector members are rejected. Whole film picture/audio, broader combinations, owner creative review and professional/production qualification remain separate.

Logo letter spacing supports signed drafts: Enter/blur commits; Escape or locking discards an uncommitted draft. The new blank entry prepares an eight-second canvas through the same upload, ownership and entitlement path as other Studio sources.

common_errors.resolution: Check source ownership, required features and current processing state. Review and regenerate only through the existing workflow.
